function parse(self, infix) result(ans)
        class(parser_t) :: self
        character(*) :: infix
        type(token_list) :: tokens
        type(token_list) :: postfix
        type(token_list) :: output
        type(token_t)    :: ans

        self % tokenizer % validate_token => by_expression
        tokens = self % tokenizer % tokenize(infix)

        if (is_enclosed(tokens)) then
            call self % convert_to_RPN(tokens, postfix)
            call self % eval_expression(postfix, output)
        else
            write(error_unit,*) 'Unmatched parenthesis on: '//infix
            stop
        end if
        ans = output % pop()
    contains
        logical function by_expression(token)
            character(*), intent(in) :: token
            by_expression = .true. &
            .and. .not. is_ignored(token) &
            .and. ( &
                     is_unary(token) &
                .or. is_binary(token) &
                .or. is_operand(token) &
                .or. is_open_paren(token) &
                .or. is_close_paren(token) &
            )
        end function
    end function

scope: Token-based expression parsing with user-supplied callbacks. The main checks precedence, parentheses, right-associative exponentiation, square root and unary minus against five exact results. A checksum-guarded edit moves a host-independent library callback to module scope after the original layout crashed in the sandbox; parsing rules are unchanged. The author documents global registrations, fixed precedences and missing syntax validation; concurrent parsers and malformed expressions are not supported by this example.
compatibility_edits: Move by_expression from an internal function of parse to a module procedure. It uses no host variables. The callback tests and parsing rules are unchanged; the original sandbox crash is retained.
known_limitations: The author documents global token registrations, fixed operator precedence, and missing syntax validation. The checked main uses one parser and valid expressions only.
